relations.myth: The king travels through Shu and traverses Aker
relations.note: The deceased king passes through Shu before traversing Aker.

relations.myth: Aker’s and Geb’s doors open for the king
relations.note: Their doors open in parallel, permitting the deceased king’s emergence.

relations.myth: Anubis calls the king forth from Aker
relations.note: Anubis’s voice enables the deceased king to emerge through Aker’s opened doors.

relations.myth: The emerged king becomes an akh like Thoth
relations.note: After leaving Aker, the king becomes an effective spirit modeled on Thoth.

relations.myth: Horus prevents Aker from seizing the king
relations.note: Horus removes the deceased’s bonds so Aker cannot lay hold of him.
The collective Akeru are said to have existed before Geb.

relations.myth: Ra passes through Aker during the solar night
relations.note: Ra travels through Aker’s earth-body and is delivered toward sunrise.
relations.source: Ramesside Books of the Earth, KV9

relations.myth: Khepri rises from the terrestrial horizon
relations.note: The renewed morning sun emerges as Khepri from Aker’s horizon complex.
relations.source: Book of the Dead and royal iconography

relations.myth: Yesterday and Tomorrow frame Osirian and solar renewal
relations.note: Osiris represents Yesterday within the two-lion horizon theology associated with Aker.

relations.myth: The paired lions are identified as Shu and Tefnut
relations.note: Spell 17 exegesis identifies one of Aker-Ruty’s paired lions with Shu.
relations.source: Book of the Dead Spell 17 commentary

relations.myth: The paired lions are identified as Shu and Tefnut
relations.note: Spell 17 exegesis identifies one of Aker-Ruty’s paired lions with Tefnut.
relations.source: Book of the Dead Spell 17 commentary

relations.myth: Aker’s opposed form overlaps with Ruty
relations.note: Aker’s double earth form is iconographically and conceptually assimilated to Ruty.
relations.source: Middle and New Kingdom funerary tradition

relations.myth: Aker encloses the hidden Sokarian cavern
relations.note: Aker’s double-sphinx form borders the subterranean cavern ruled by Sokar.

relations.myth: Aker contains Apophis in the terrestrial underworld
relations.note: Aker supplies the containing earth while other divine agents attack Apophis.

relations.myth: Aker lies beneath paired images of Nut
relations.note: KV9 arranges Aker as earth below and Nut as the complementary sky above.

relations.myth: Heka accompanies the solar setting above Aker
relations.note: Later objects show Heka supporting Nut or accompanying the bark above Aker imagery.
